body:
HandleSyncRequest prunes expired pending pages (kobo.py:720-727, PENDING_SYNC_PAGE_TTL=7d in kobo_sync_status.py:18) BEFORE looking up the page the incoming token acknowledges. With a resolved device id, KoboSyncedBooks rows / ledger fingerprints / rehydrate-latch clears / removed-book deletions are written only via _acknowledge_pending_page, which fires on the device's NEXT sync. A Kobo idle >7 days (drawer/holiday device) therefore loses the confirmation of its session's final page every time.

Damage: (a) books on the lost page get no ledger fingerprint -> replay suppression ineligible -> byte-identical re-emission, which the code's own comment (kobo.py:2157-2161) identifies as the proven Nickel de-download trigger #1925 fixed; (b) single-device users can re-enter the KoboSyncedBooks-empty full reset (:782) on return, re-arming every position latch; (c) a stuck rehydrate_needed makes the cover-reset guard (:2615-2632) reject genuine <=1% restarts and push the old position back.

CONFIDENCE: likely. Settle by staging a page, aging created_at 8 days, presenting its outgoing token, observing prune-before-ack and NewEntitlement re-emission. Source: adversarial audit state/kobo-audit-2026-09-01.
title: 7-day pending-page TTL prunes the ack before it can be processed; the session's last page becomes replay-suppression-ineligible and re-arms the #1925 de-download hazard
